analysis: Market context: The broader market has stabilized after tariff-driven volatility. Many S&P 500 quality names are basing 10-30% below their 52-week highs — classic Stage 1→2 transition territory. Portfolio is essentially all-cash ($100k) with one negligible NNDM position, giving us clean slate to deploy into 3 high-conviction setups. Strategy: concentrate into quality names with compelling valuations that are technically basing (not falling), where the downside is capped by both a hard stop and the fundamental value floor. Selected three names with different sector exposure (fintech, technology, healthcare) for diversification without dilution. PYPL is the top-ranked setup — cheapest quality fintech with accelerating SMA50 momentum. MSFT is the long-term compounder at a rare fair entry. CI is deep-value healthcare with contained downside. Total deployment ~75% of equity; 25% remains cash as a buffer. Avoiding COIN (high ATR, revenue -22%), PANW (expensive, extended), APP (MIXED trend, highly extended prior peak), and ADSK (negative SMA50 slope). Win rate shows 0W/0L on 12 trades — suggests those trades never hit stops or targets; maintaining disciplined entries here.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $50.44 (current price) or better on any intraday pullback. Ideal add on retest of SMA50 (~$46.70) if market dips. Requires price to hold above 20-day low.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: PayPal trades at P/E 9.32 (fwd 8.71) with PEG 0.91 — deeply undervalued for a franchise generating $3.3B FCF and $6.4B operating cash flow. ROE 25.7% signals a capital-light business. New CEO focus on branded checkout conversion rates and Venmo monetization is showing early traction in the 3.7% revenue growth. At 30% of 52-week range with $38.96 support well below, the valuation floor is credible. TECHNICAL: UPTREND (basing) confirmation with SMA50 slope +2.3% over 20 days — the strongest positive slope among top candidates. Price is +8% above SMA50 (not yet extended). Lower half of range at 30% — Stage 1→2 transition setup. The risk/reward of 5.35x makes this the highest-priority entry.
trades.exit_plan: Hard stop $47.72 (2x ATR below entry). Trim 40% of position near $60 to de-risk. Full thesis break: if SMA50 slope turns negative for 3+ consecutive weeks, or if FCF guidance is cut meaningfully at next earnings. Time stop: reassess after 90 days if price has not moved toward $58+.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $412-414 near current price. Ideal entry on any pullback toward SMA50 (~$396). Do not chase above $425.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Microsoft is the highest-quality business in the candidate universe — 46.3% operating margins, $37B FCF, ROE 34%, $170B operating cash flow, D/E only 30. Forward P/E 21.45 with PEG 1.29 is a fair price for a secular compounder. Azure cloud revenue growing double-digits; Copilot AI integration deepening switching costs across Office 365 and enterprise. 18.3% revenue growth at this scale is exceptional. TECHNICAL: Basing at 32% of 52-week range after tariff-driven macro selloff — the business has not deteriorated, only the multiple compressed. Price +4.6% above SMA50. The mixed trend reflects macro noise; SMA50 is stabilizing. This is an accumulation opportunity in a world-class business at a fair price, not a falling knife.
trades.exit_plan: Hard stop $395.79. Intend to hold past 12 months for LTCG if thesis intact — Azure growth, Copilot adoption, FCF expansion. Trim 30% near $470. Thesis break: if Azure growth decelerates below 15% YoY for two consecutive quarters, or if AI monetization fails to show in margins. Do not sell on macro headlines alone.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $282 or better. Accept fill up to $285. Prefer entry on a green day when market is stable — avoid entering into healthcare policy headline risk days.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Cigna Group is one of the cheapest quality healthcare names — forward P/E 8.44, PEG 0.82, FCF $6.9B, Op CF $8.8B. The Evernorth PBM division drives 23.5% revenue growth at scale. P/B 1.79 and ROE 16.3% suggest a capital-efficient franchise trading at a significant discount to intrinsic value. Managed care medical cost ratio headwinds are partially priced in; Cigna's PBM-heavy mix provides relative insulation versus pure insurers. D/E 72 is manageable given strong cash flows. TECHNICAL: Basing at 47% of 52-week range, price +1.1% above SMA200 (long-term trend floor holding), and SMA50 slope -0.3% (essentially flat — stabilizing after a downtrend). Consolidating above key support $275. Not the cleanest technical setup but valuation provides a large margin of safety that reduces dependence on perfect timing.
trades.exit_plan: Hard stop $271.44. Exit if medical cost ratio guidance increases materially at next earnings print, or if Evernorth revenue growth turns negative. Time stop: 90 days; if stock has not shown upward progress toward $295, reassess thesis. Consider holding past 12 months for LTCG if fundamentals remain intact.
